old_title: Live: Payne Haas scores a try, gets binned in final Broncos game against Dogs
new_title: Broncos send Haas out a winner with top score of 2026 against Dogs
old_text:
live
NRL live: Canterbury Bulldogs host Brisbane Broncos in Payne Haas's farewell
The Bulldogs host the Broncos in a final-round contest between two teams that fell well below expectations in the 2026 NRL season.
The game marks superstar prop Payne Haas's final outing for Brisbane before he heads to the Rabbitohs next season.
Follow all the action in our live blog below, check out all the stats in the full ScoreCentre, and tune in to our live radio coverage.
Submit a comment or question
Live updates
Live: Bulldogs vs Broncos at Homebush
New: Filters
Choose what information you see below by using filters
The Broncos start the second half hot
Pat Carrigan offloads in the middle of the field and Billy Walters wastes no time firing the ball out wide, where Kotoni Staggs unleashes Grant Anderson down the right wing.
Walters backs up through the middle and gets it back to score.
44' Josiah Karapani is having a worldie
He's been immense under the high ball, near enough to flawless in fact, and can't be stopped when it's in his hands.
He's just had his 10th tackle bust and he's already approach 100 metres.
41' The Broncos start off the second half
Harry Hayes charges back for the Bulldogs.
Key Event
HALF-TIME: It's tied 10-10 at the break
The Bulldogs plays some audacious attacking football to end the half but Jacob Preston's grubber ends up with the Broncos and the whistle is blown.
An entertaining half of football, with both sides showing why they're not in the finals and giving glimpses as to why that frustrates their fans so much.
Key Event
The Dogs are over to tie it up
The left-side shift is unlocked with Viliame Kikau digging into the line and sending a ball back to Stephen Crichton, who throws a lovely cut-out pass to Enari Tuala to score.
That was a bad read by Grant Anderson, who came too far in from his wing.
Stephen Crichton hooks the sideline conversion, so it's 10-10 with four minutes until half-time.
33' Hayze Perham saves the day
Jacob Preston explodes onto a Lachie Galvin short ball and into open space as he's done so many times before. He comes to fullback Hayze Perham with AJ Jones on his left, tries to draw and pass but Perham shoots the gap and bats it down.
A near certain try goes begging.
31' Ezra Mam throws a shocker
The Broncos make a break through the middle courtesy of another Payne Haas offload to Billy Walters, who unleashes Ezra Mam.
He finds himself in open space with no-one around, so he flings it out to the left, but there's no-one there!
26' Almost a very nasty accident
The bomb goes up and Connor Tracey leaps high to take it as Deine Mariner arrives to corral him.
But Mariner's feet slip out from under him as he arrives and he goes right under Tracey, whose boot collects Mariner's face, but mercifully a proper disaster is averted.
23' Broncos choose to receive
Brisbane isn't involved in the silent protest against the kick-off rule trial as, with Payne Haas still in the bin, the Broncos choose to receive the kick-off.
And they get a piggyback as Jacob Preston is dubiously penalised for a crusher tackle on Ezra Mam.
Key Event
Lachie Galvin dives in for the Dogs
The Broncos' flimsy left side concedes yet another try as Lachlan Galvin sets sail for the yawning gap between Jaiyden Hunt and Ezra Mam.
The outside men over-read and Galvin coasts through as Hunt fails to close the gap.
19' Bulldogs reject possession
The Bulldogs have the option to receive the kick-off after conceding points under this new rule the NRL is trialling.
But the silent protest is on, it seems, as the Dogs refuse it despite surely wanting every attacking opportunity possible against 12 men.
Everyone hates this rule aside from Peter V'landys it seems.
Key Event
The Broncos score with 12 men!
Ben Hunt's attempted floater bomb is hooked shallow across field and Jacob Kiraz can't handle as Josiah Karapani leaps through and regathers the bobble.
There's a question of Karapani's actions though. Did he get a hand to it as Kiraz fumbled it?
The try is confirmed! Hayze Perham hooks his conversion and the Broncos lead 10-0 after 18 minutes.
Key Event
15' Payne Haas is in the sin bin!
From the penthouse to the outhouse for big Haas as he commits the Broncos' third straight ruck infringement while they defend their line and he has to go for 10 minutes.
I'm not sure the first two were the correct calls, but Haas left the referee with not option when he refused to let go of Leo Thompson right under the posts.
Key Event
Payne Haas says goodbye to the Broncos with a try!
The Broncos get their first good field position as Jacob Kiraz forces a terrible offload and Josiah Karapani comes up with it.
They rumble up the middle, earn a set restart and Payne Haas gets the ball 10 metres out, trampling Bailey Hayward, slipping out of Viliame Kikau's tackle and carrying Connor Tracey and Leo Thompson as he slams the ball down under the posts.
Key Event
1' Bulldogs kick off
Xavier Willison, the heir apparent to Payne Haas, takes the first hit-up.
And already the Broncos looking disjointed as Billy Walters tries to kick out of dummy half on the fourth and Pat Carrigan gets in his way.
And then Ben Hunt scuffs his bomb to end the set.
Payne Haas leads the Broncos out
The teams are on their way onto the field, starting with the soon-to-be Rabbitoh.
And here come the Bulldogs, led by Stephen Crichton.
Kick-off isn't far away
Who are you picking?
I've got the Bulldogs winning comfortably.
'You're remembered by what you do now': Maguire on motivation for Broncos
There's nothing but pride to play for for both these teams, but that should be plenty, according to Brisbane coach Michael Maguire.
"It's a game you're gonna be remembered by. Your teammates out there know exactly what goes on. You're rememebered by what you do now by your teammates, by your fans and your coaches."
The Broncos have a little extra motivation to send Payne Haas out a winner.
"He's a great man and he's given a lot to the club. The boys have really enjoyed the week together."
And it's another milestone ticked off for Ben Hunt, as he plays his 373rd NRL game to pass Cooper Cronk for outright third.
"He's been a major part of what has gone on in the club. To see Benny come back and lead it's what he does away from the field. They're the things most people don't get to see."
Payne's last ride
After the debacle that was the Adam Reynolds Lang Park farewell, the Broncos are having another crack at it as Souths-bound Payne Haas plays his final game for Brisbane before heading to Redfern for 2027.
It doesn't feel right that such a champion leaves this club in such underwhelming circumstances, but perhaps we'll see one last iconic outing from him in maroon and gold tonight.

Brisbane Broncos beat Canterbury Bulldogs 34-20 in Payne Haas's farewell
The Broncos have won a final-round contest against the Bulldogs 34-20, in a game that doubled as superstar prop Payne Haas's farewell from Brisbane.
Haas scored the opening try as the Broncos notched up their equal highest score of a disappointing 2026 season, tied with their tally from a 34-30 win over the Raiders four weeks earlier.
Halfback Ben Hunt said the team had extra motivation to send Haas out a winner before he heads to South Sydney from 2027.
"Payne means a hell of a lot to this club, he really does," Hunt told ABC Sport.
"It's been a very disappointing year, but to come out here tonight, the boys really carried themselves in a great way and really showed up for Payne.
"He deserved the win tonight."
The teams were tied 10-10 at half-time, but the Broncos, sparked by Hunt and hooker Billy Walters, exploded after the break with four tries in 15 minutes to jump out to a 24-point lead.
Canterbury hit back with tries to Viliame Kikau and Lachlan Galvin, but they could not get close enough to truly challenge the Broncos, who will finish 14th or 15th in their failed premiership defence.
Look back all the action in our live blog below, and check out all the stats in the full ScoreCentre.

That's where we'll leave you
We'll be back tomorrow night for Titans-Dolphins and Rabbitohs-Roosters, featuring what will no doubt be another emotional tribute to Jai Arrow.
Join us then.
I can't believe this is how it ends
Payne Haas has played his last game in a Broncos jersey (For now, go the cries from Brisbane fans) and he's done it in a dead-rubber in front of 13,000 fans in Sydney.
For a duo like him and Pat Carrigan to end like this just feels wrong.
And Adam Reynolds is heading for retirement. Such a huge part of the core of the 2025 premiership team is gone.
Canterbury coach Cameron Ciraldo is miserable
The Bulldogs coach is not happy with that performance.
"We had a lot to play for. It's been a tough up and down year. We wanted to finish the year strong. I expected us to put in our best performance of the year and we were a long way off that.
"Everything we did this week was about getting our best performance tonight and I'm shattered we didn't."
Are you listening, Reece?
Key Event
FULL-TIME: The Broncos close out 2026 with victory over the Bulldogs
So it ends 34-20 to the Broncos, which is the equal-most points they've scored all year, tied with their round 23 tally against the Raiders.
Halfback Ben Hunt says they did it for Payne Haas before he sets sail for Redfern.
"Payne means a hell of a lot to this club. It's been a disappointing year but the boys carried themselves really well."
79' An absolute bottle job
The Broncos have a 4 vs 1 on the right and they manage to bomb it as Hayze Perham throws a no-look pass.
75' Bulldogs get the kick-off back after a ridiculous bounce
The short kick-off is well short, bounces even further back, but then goes forward for two bounces and the Bulldogs regather in front of a shell-shocked Broncos side.
The luck is turning.
Key Event
Galvin scores and the Dogs are coming
Lachie Galvin's grubber takes a deflection and Grant Anderson can't clean up, with the halfback regathering the ricochet to score.
Stephen Crichton leaves the conversion wide left, so they still trail 34-20 with five six minutes left.
72' Ben Hunt comes up with another play
He goes for the 40/20 from dummy half and Connor Tracey is forced to bat it back into play, but he can only knock it dead.
But it's a galaxy brain play as it turns out, because they've regathered the short dropout through Jacob Kiraz and got a piggyback penalty for a crusher tackle.
The Dogs are over
Viliame Kikau scores a brilliant barnstorming try after a monster fend on Tom Duffy.
And the broncos have chosen to receive the kick-off as the Bulldogs finally arrive in the second half.
63' The Broncos have an all-timer taken off them
The Bulldogs spin it right to get out of their own red zone and Lachlan Galvin launches it back left to Stephen Crichton, who fires another long ball, but Grant Anderson flies out of nowhere to intercept.
He gets caught and spun around by the defence as he looks to offload.
Eventually Tom Duffy arrives, but by that point Anderosn has to offload behind his back, and he's thrown it forward!
Duffy raced away to score, and only realised it had been called forward after he got up to celebrate.
Key Event
Josiah Karapani is over for another Broncos try
This is getting out of hand as the Bulldogs surrender possession and Grant Anderson tip-toes up the sideline to get them flying upfield.
Ben Hunt again chips over early in the count and Josiah Karapani catches on the full, but a stumble stops him from scoring.
So he simply reloads and orchestrates a more straightforward left-side shift, ending in a stunning putdown by Karapani.
His impressive night just gets better.
Key Event
The Broncos are pouring it on
Ben Hunt comes up with what looks like a little improvisational play, propping off his left foot on the left side of the field to catch the Bulldogs' defence napping.
He kicks high into a vacant zone behind the left flank and it's perfectly weighted for Jordan Riki to catch and score.
Ben Hunt joins the party
And it's a trademark Hunt try in his 373rd NRL game as he jags back hard off his right foot to bamboozle Stephen Crichton and Viliame Kikau.
He bumps off Connor Tracey and the Broncos have the first two tries of the second half.
47' Broncos regather off the kick-off
The Bulldogs utilise the new rule and choose to receive, but the Broncos land it in no man's land and manage to regather.

Pat Carrigan offloads in the middle of the field and Billy Walters wastes no time firing the ball out wide, where Kotoni Staggs unleashes Grant Anderson down the right wing.
Walters backs up through the middle and gets it back to score.

Harry Hayes charges back for the Bulldogs.

An entertaining half of football, with both sides showing why they're not in the finals and giving glimpses as to why that frustrates their fans so much.
